items.title: Require a recorded dev-memory preflight acknowledgement before a story may enter DEV
items.context: Mirrors the existing scope_boundary_set/execution_boundary_set/scope_freeze_check INIT_CHECK-gating pattern. New command (e.g. dev_memory_preflight_ack) writes a JSON artifact under .lattice/story/actives/<id>/ recording that dev_memory_preflight was run and its topHitIds were seen; the DEV-entry gate refuses to advance without this artifact present and bound to the current story's material.

happy.desc: Story in PLAN with no dev-memory-preflight-ack.json artifact -> call dev_memory_preflight_ack -> artifact written -> canStartDevGuard allows PLAN->DEV transition; WHY: confirms the primary happy path (ack exists -> gate opens)

evaluateDevMemoryPreflightGate returns true when a valid dev-memory-preflight-ack.json exists for the story, regardless of its packDigest/topHitIds content; WHY: existence-only check per plan (not hash/staleness-bound)

getGuardFailureReason for targetPhase=DEV includes missing_dev_memory_preflight_ack tag and actionable run-command hint when ack artifact is absent; WHY: confirms user-visible error message is helpful

edge.desc: Story re-entering DEV from REVIEW (canReenterDevGuard) with ack already present from first PLAN->DEV entry -> gate passes with zero added friction; WHY: ack persists for story lifetime, rollback doors must not re-prompt
Story skipping PLAN (canSkipPlanGuard) still requires the ack artifact and blocks without it; WHY: all four DEV doors must be gated, not just the PLAN->DEV path

dev_memory_preflight_ack writes artifact with correct schema (schemaVersion, storyId, packDigest, topHitIds, acknowledgedAt, acknowledgedBy) and is readable by evaluateDevMemoryPreflightGate; WHY: round-trip data integrity

adversarial.desc: All four DEV-entry doors (canStartDevGuard, canSkipPlanGuard, canReenterDevGuard from REVIEW, canReenterDevGuard from TEST) block when dev-memory-preflight-ack.json is absent; WHY: adversarial check that gate is wired into EVERY door, not just the primary PLAN->DEV path the story emphasizes

Deleting/truncating dev-memory-preflight-ack.json after it was written -> evaluateDevMemoryPreflightGate returns false (fail-closed, treats missing/corrupt as blocking); WHY: prevents bypass via file deletion or corruption

dev-memory-preflight-ack.json containing invalid JSON (e.g. truncated, empty object {}, wrong schemaVersion) -> evaluateDevMemoryPreflightGate treats it as absent (fail-closed); WHY: a corrupt or hand-crafted artifact must not satisfy the gate

items.title: Append a non-blocking dev-memory capture reminder to finding_resolve output
items.context: After finding_resolve completes, append advisory text (does not block, does not mutate anything else) prompting the caller to consider dev_memory_capture for the finding's root cause/fix if it represents a genuinely reusable lesson.

happy.desc: Call finding_resolve for a valid finding -> output string contains advisory text mentioning dev_memory_capture; WHY: confirms the reminder is appended to the normal finding_resolve output
Advisory text appears as a suffix after the existing commitHint in the output template literal, not replacing it; WHY: must not clobber the existing auto-commit advisory

edge.desc: finding_resolve on a finding with no reusable lesson context (trivial typo fix) -> advisory text still appears (it is unconditional, the agent decides whether to act on it); WHY: advisory is a reminder, not a smart filter -- it should always appear

finding_resolve called when memory subsystem has zero experience entries (empty experience.jsonl) -> advisory text still renders without error; WHY: empty-memory edge case must not crash the pack builder
Advisory text does NOT appear in any non-finding_resolve command output (e.g. finding_record, finding_list) -> scoped only to finding_resolve; WHY: prevents advisory fatigue from over-broad placement

adversarial.desc: Memory subsystem throws (e.g. corrupt experience.jsonl, missing .lattice/dev-memory directory, packBuilder exception) during finding_resolve -> finding_resolve still succeeds with its normal output and exit code 0, memoryHint silently becomes empty string; WHY: the try/catch wrapper must genuinely swallow all memory-subsystem failures without blocking the primary finding_resolve operation

finding_resolve called with a finding that itself fails validation (invalid findingId) -> the memory advisory code path is never reached and does not mask the real finding_resolve error; WHY: the advisory must not interfere with normal error propagation

Concurrent finding_resolve calls (two findings resolved in rapid succession) -> both emit advisory text independently without corrupting each other or the experience.jsonl; WHY: advisory is read-only against memory state, but the pack builder may have shared state

items.title: Require a recorded dev_memory_finish_decision before a story may reach DONE
items.context: Add to canFinishGuard (core/machine.ts) or wherever the DONE checklist is assembled: require a dev_memory_finish_decision record for the story, accepting captured | no-reusable-lesson | defer-with-reason as satisfying answers. Mirrors how summary_set/delivery-check are already required DONE items.

happy.desc: Story with no finish-decision record -> canFinishGuard returns false and getGuardFailureReason emits missing_dev_memory_finish_decision tag with actionable run-command hint; WHY: confirms DONE gate blocks when record is absent
Call dev_memory_finish_decision with decision=captured -> canFinishGuard passes for this check; WHY: positive capture satisfies gate
Call dev_memory_finish_decision with decision=no-reusable-lesson -> canFinishGuard passes for this check; WHY: honest negative is explicitly valid per design
Call dev_memory_finish_decision with decision=defer-with-reason -> canFinishGuard passes for this check; WHY: deferred-with-reason is explicitly valid per design

edge.desc: readDevMemoryFinishDecision lives in core/playbook-runtime-memory.ts and is imported by core/machine.ts as a core->core import (not core->handlers); WHY: architectural constraint from plan -- no new core->handlers inversions

handlers/playbook-runtime-memory.ts dev_memory_finish_decision writer imports finishDecisionPath from core module instead of defining it locally; WHY: single source of truth for the path, no duplicate definitions

canFinishGuard checks finish-decision AFTER existing test-evidence check (lines 877-882 pattern), so a story missing test evidence still fails on test-evidence first, not on finish-decision; WHY: guard ordering must not mask more fundamental blockers

adversarial.desc: finish-decision JSON file exists but contains invalid JSON (truncated, empty string, random bytes) -> readDevMemoryFinishDecision returns null -> canFinishGuard returns false (fail-closed); WHY: corrupt/hand-crafted artifact must not bypass the DONE gate

finish-decision JSON file exists but has wrong schema (e.g. missing decision field, decision=invented-value not in captured|no-reusable-lesson|defer-with-reason) -> gate treats as unsatisfied; WHY: prevents gaming with arbitrary file content

finish-decision file for a DIFFERENT storyId placed at the current story path -> readDevMemoryFinishDecision either rejects on storyId mismatch or the path-builder already namespaces by storyId making cross-story injection impossible; WHY: cross-story artifact reuse must not satisfy the gate
Deleting finish-decision file after it was written and re-checking canFinishGuard -> gate blocks again (no caching); WHY: gate must re-read from disk each time, not cache a previous positive result

items.title: Add a new smoke test covering all three dev-memory lifecycle gates, registered in validate.commands
items.context: New file packages/main/src/tasks/dev-memory-lifecycle-gates-smoke.ts, covering CHK-001's DEV-door refusal-then-pass across all four doors (including the reasoned-downgrade --reason path), CHK-002's advisory text presence/absence and fail-safe-under-throw behavior, and CHK-003's DONE-gate refusal-then-pass for all three decision values plus the fail-closed corrupt-record case. Register in lattice.config.json validate.commands.

happy.desc: Run `node packages/main/dist/tasks/dev-memory-lifecycle-gates-smoke.js` -> exits 0 with all assertions passing; WHY: confirms the smoke test itself is a valid, complete, passing test that exercises real gate logic

Smoke test contains refusal-then-pass assertions for CHK-001 DEV-door gating: all four doors (canStartDevGuard, canSkipPlanGuard, canReenterDevGuard from REVIEW, canReenterDevGuard from TEST) return false when ack artifact is absent, then return true after dev_memory_preflight_ack writes the artifact; WHY: covers CHK-001 both-halves across all doors

Smoke test contains assertions for CHK-002 advisory behavior: finding_resolve output includes dev_memory_capture advisory text after successful resolve, AND memory subsystem throw does not break finding_resolve (exit 0, advisory silently becomes empty string); WHY: covers CHK-002 happy + fail-safe

Smoke test contains DONE-gate assertions for CHK-003: canFinishGuard returns false with no finish-decision record, then returns true for each of decision=captured, decision=no-reusable-lesson, decision=defer-with-reason, AND returns false for corrupt/invalid JSON finish-decision file; WHY: covers CHK-003 full decision matrix plus fail-closed corruption case

edge.desc: Smoke test is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands with the exact compiled path `packages/main/dist/tasks/dev-memory-lifecycle-gates-smoke.js` matching the existing registration pattern; WHY: unregistered test is never run by validate and provides zero assurance

Smoke test covers the section-4.3-compliant --reason bypass/downgrade path for CHK-001: when pack build throws AND --reason is provided, ack artifact is written with packDigest:null/topHitIds:[] and gate still passes; WHY: the reasoned-downgrade path is a plan-level requirement distinct from the normal preflight path

Smoke test uses mkdtempSync + git init temp fixture pattern (matching codebase convention e.g. quorum-submit-smoke.ts makeFixture) and does not leak temp directories on success or assertion failure; WHY: shared CI environment accumulation / cross-test contamination

adversarial.desc: Smoke test contains genuine refusal-THEN-pass assertion pairs for EVERY gate (not just write-artifact-then-assert-passes): each gate is first asserted false/blocking without the artifact, then true/passing after the artifact is written -- grep source for the refusal assertion before the write call; WHY: a test that only checks the pass-after-write path would pass vacuously even if the gate function were a no-op returning true unconditionally

Smoke test explicitly names and invokes all 4 DEV-entry doors (canStartDevGuard, canSkipPlanGuard, canReenterDevGuard with previousPhase REVIEW, canReenterDevGuard with previousPhase TEST) -- grep source confirms all four; WHY: a test covering only PLAN->DEV leaves 3 doors untested, which is the exact gap CHK-001 adversarial-intent-3 is designed to catch

Smoke test source file exists at packages/main/src/tasks/dev-memory-lifecycle-gates-smoke.ts AND lattice.config.json validate.commands contains an entry pointing to the compiled dist/ path -- both must be present simultaneously; WHY: source without registration means the test never runs in validate (silently passing CI with zero coverage)

Smoke test CHK-002 fail-safe coverage includes a concrete throw-path test (e.g. corrupt experience.jsonl or missing .lattice/dev-memory dir causing pack builder to throw) where finding_resolve still completes without error -- not just testing that advisory text appears on the happy path; WHY: the fail-safe-under-throw property is the critical adversarial guarantee of CHK-002, and testing only the happy path would miss a try/catch that silently swallows the wrong exception or re-throws

items.title: Update the pre-existing playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md spec doc to describe the delivered/escalated CHK-003 behavior
items.context: M8 'Capture-Or-Noop Decision' currently describes dev_memory_finish_decision as advisory-only ('missing decision is visible in runbook/advisory output'). Update that section to describe the actually-delivered behavior: this story deliberately escalates ONE specific consumer (the DONE gate) to blocking, while preserving the original advisory text as historical rationale (mirrors B-3144's docs/evidence-write-guard-spec.md 'Delivered differently' pattern). Also document that this is the first concrete instance of section 4.3's registered-blocking-consumer-with-operator-visible-bypass-path pattern being exercised for a dev-memory consumer, satisfied via the existing reason-required decision/downgrade-ack values (no new bypass mechanism needed).

happy.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md M8 section now describes dev_memory_finish_decision as a blocking DONE-gate requirement (contains words like "blocking" or "required" in the context of DONE/canFinishGuard), not purely advisory; WHY: confirms the primary update was made -- the M8 section must reflect the actually-delivered escalation

The updated M8 section preserves the original advisory-only text as historical rationale (via a "Delivered differently" callout, "Historical note" block, or equivalent clearly-marked subsection), not deleted or overwritten; WHY: confirms the B-3144 "Delivered differently" pattern was followed as required by the plan

The doc documents section 4.3 registered-blocking-consumer-with-bypass-path pattern being exercised for the first time by a dev-memory consumer, satisfied via the existing reason-required decision values (captured/no-reusable-lesson/defer-with-reason) with no new bypass mechanism introduced; WHY: confirms the 4.3 precedent documentation was added as the plan requires

edge.desc: The original M8 acceptance test text ("missing decision is visible in runbook/advisory output") is still present somewhere in the document as historical context, not replaced or deleted; WHY: plan explicitly requires preserving original text -- a reviewer grepping for that exact phrase must still find it

The doc references the actual mechanism names matching shipped code: dev_memory_finish_decision, captured, no-reusable-lesson, defer-with-reason, canFinishGuard -- not placeholder/generic names; WHY: doc-code name divergence is a known high-severity finding pattern (B-3144 F-030 stale spec)

The doc does NOT add new bypass mechanisms or new decision values beyond what the code ships (no invented values like "skip" or "override" that do not exist in the codebase) -- it only describes what is actually delivered; WHY: doc-code divergence creates false expectations for the next implementer reading the spec

adversarial.desc: The original M8 section advisory-only text is NOT deleted or overwritten -- diff the file against main branch to confirm the pre-existing advisory text (e.g. "missing decision is visible in runbook/advisory output") still appears in the file, possibly inside a historical-rationale block; WHY: user explicitly flagged losing/deleting the original rationale as an adversarial failure mode

The doc update does NOT describe the DONE gate as advisory-only when the code makes it blocking, or describe it as blocking in contexts where it is actually advisory -- the doc description of blocking vs advisory behavior must match the actual canFinishGuard code path; WHY: user explicitly flagged contradicting the shipped code as an adversarial failure mode

The doc update is committed to the branch (git log --oneline --diff-filter=M -- docs/requirements/decisions/playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md shows at least one commit on the branch touching this file), not merely described in chat output; WHY: user explicitly flagged not-actually-committed as an adversarial failure mode
